submission.justification: Sensor-T3 gives the best unirradiated resolution (6.0 um at 150 um in the 2025 summary), but after 2e16 neq/cm^2 its hit efficiency falls to 82.0% because of strong charge trapping and it cannot reach full depletion. That fails the >=97% end-of-life requirement, so it is excluded. Sensor-T1 (98.5%) and Sensor-T2 (99.2%) both meet the radiation requirement. Among these, T1 gives the better resolution at every thickness simulated. A thickness scan of T1 (unirradiated, 100k events) gave 10.3 um at 50 um, 9.2 um at 100 um, 8.8 um at 150 um, 9.4 um at 200 um and 12.4 um at 300 um, so the optimum is near 150 um. T2 gave 13.6 to 14.9 um over 100 to 200 um, so it is worse. Caveat: the resolution figures are unirradiated, and the irradiated resolution at 150 um was not simulated. Thickness choice should be confirmed against irradiated performance before pre-production.

requirements.requirement: Sensor must be one of the three candidate technologies
requirements.evidence: Sensor-T1 is a candidate listed in candidate_specs.md (planar, standard pitch).

requirements.requirement: Suitable for innermost-layer radiation environment (>=97% hit efficiency up to 2e16 neq/cm^2)
requirements.evidence: irradiation_testbeam_2026.md: Sensor-T1 98.5% after 2e16 neq/cm^2. Sensor-T3 (82.0%) fails and was excluded.

T1 at 150 um: 8.84 um unirradiated, the best of the radiation-qualified options (T2 at 150 um: 13.56 um). Scan of T1 from 50 to 300 um showed a minimum near 150 um. T3 (6.0 um in 2025 summary) is better but not radiation-qualified.

requirements.requirement: Finish by submitting one recommended technology and thickness
